rationale: Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-067 (illustrative figures), A-1 (binding): market rents keep rising faster than 1.8% a year, so the cap binds within the first year.
WE-067 A-2 (enforcement): the board enforces the cap against most landlords.
WE-067 A-12 (alternative_uses): the withdrawal route is used for a meaningful number of buildings.
WE-067 A-3: covered tenancies cannot be assigned or sold, and sublets are limited to the tenant's rent.
WE-067 A-28: buyouts move fewer keepers out of their units than the cap and the for-cause rule hold in place.
WE-067 A-6 (mobility): without the ordinance some sitting tenants would have left Tessford, priced out or for opportunities elsewhere.
WE-067 A-31: for non-qualifying keepers the lock-in from forfeiting the gap outweighs any diversion of their moves by higher free rents (the dominance premise PC-21 asks for).
WE-067 A-26: by the third year the cap cuts non-qualifying keepers' moves out of Tessford by more than the displaced non-senior households add.
WE-067 A-22 (substitutability): covered and exempt Tessford units are close substitutes.
No row. WE-067 section 2: under vacancy decontrol PC-2 does not apply; seekers pay a free initial rent and are not rationed. Estimate from the record.
No row. Same as search_open: no rationing at a capped price for new tenancies. Estimate from the record.
WE-067 A-10: the housing code leaves room to cut maintenance above the legal minimum.
WE-067 A-11 (enforcement): some sublets above the controlled rent go undetected.
WE-067 A-25 (mobility): some job opportunities for sitting tenants would require leaving the unit.
WE-067 A-18: landlords, tenant unions and senior advocates can organize at a cost below their stakes.
WE-067 A-13 (durability): rental buildings last several decades, so the stock changes slowly.
WE-067 A-23 (expectations): buyers of buildings expect the ordinance to last many years.
WE-067 A-15 (mobility): some seekers shut out of Tessford settle elsewhere in the county and in Durnside and commute.

WE-067 A-34 (alternative_uses, p 0.6): in a building an owner plans to withdraw, holding a vacated unit empty pays better than re-letting it (re-letting adds a household owed $8,000 or $12,000 and 120 days' or a year's notice).
No row. Section 9 requires notice and a relocation payment, not a permit or board decision; estimate from the record.
WE-067 A-4 (expectations): enough leases renew in the window, and landlords raise rents at renewal to lift the base.
WE-067 A-5: without the ordinance sitting tenants' rents would follow the market within one or two lease cycles, so the counterfactual passes any pre-emptive raise.

Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-067 (illustrative figures), A-19: rent regulation would have been contested on the counterfactual path (election pledges in November 2026; the failed 2022 petition).
evidence: In November 2026 a majority of the newly elected council and the mayor campaigned on rent regulation.
